newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela starts probe of officials' trips.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela starts probe of officials' trips.

text.p: Venezuela's Congress started an investigation on Tuesday into the use of government jets by public officials after it was revealed that ministers may have used the planes for family holidays.
"We want to find out whether these flights are necessary," said Deputy Luis Carlos Sera Carmona, president of the commission created to study the issue.
The investigation follows reports that government ministers have used aircraft belonging to state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) for personal trips.

Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta acknowledged last week that he had given a lift to Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar and his family to Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on the way to a meeting in Washington in August.
Arrieta, who has been called to appear before the commission along with Matos and other government officials, welcomed the investigation.
"I think it will clear up many worthwhile things," he told the Globovision network.

The use of government airplanes for private reasons would be a serious embarrassment for President Rafael Caldera's government which has tried hard to distance itself from the corrupt image of previous governments.
Matos and Arrieta are key members of Caldera's cabinet.
